extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, poets, and educated readers of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for judging poetry and for conducting fair, rigorous literary criticism—covering critic impartiality, evidentiary practice, judgments about style, diction, congruity, and the poet's proper subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial administration of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics should set aside their individuality and pledge themselves to administer judgment according to a constitution and code of laws grounded on universal morals and philosophic reason, independent of all foreseen application to particular works and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fair critic speaks as representative of a corporate standard rather than a private taste; this impartiality merits respect and should be the aim of critical institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of national, party, or personal bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical verdicts must avoid the too manifest interference of national party, personal predilection or aversion, and especially criminal intrusions into private life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such improper motives occur, criticism becomes suspect; in extreme cases private invasions may merit legal rather than literary chastisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not substitute assertion for argument
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic must not merely assert conclusions; the substitution of assertion for argument is a grave fault—arbitrary and petulant verdicts are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgments should be supported by reasoning, not broad unsupported proclamations. The text criticizes reviews which begin with a vulgar exultation like 'This won't do!' without argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support judgments with textual evidence and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts and quotations should be supplied to explain the critic's meaning and to prove the justice of his sentence; verdicts unsupported even by a single quotation are weak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations must be used with reference to general grounds or rules from which the attributed faults are deduced; avoid quoting out of context or as mere illustration of preconceived opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make and announce leading principles of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics should state their own principles of judgment and support them by a connected train of reasoning rather than judging without announced premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a poet has made his principles public, a critic should engage those principles explicitly and not rely on unannounced standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure representative selection of passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages cited must be representative, not cherry-picked to illustrate preconceived conclusions; avoid selecting isolated lines with the intent to misrepresent the whole work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic who wrote his critique before reading the work and then 'pricked with a pin' for passages is accused of bad practice; selection must be fair and contextual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and contextualize defects versus beauties
rubrics_metrics.description: When pointing out defects, show how far the influence has acted: whether diffusively or by starts; whether the number and importance of defective passages are great or trifling compared with the sound portion; and whether defects are inwoven into the texture or loose and separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not condemn a whole work for a few passages; indicate proportion and relative importance—e.g., the author suggests the objectionable passages may amount to about a hundred lines in two volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine congruity of character with poetic genus
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether a character introduced (e.g., a vagrant merchant) is appropriate to the kind of poem (such as a lofty didactic poem); assess congruity or incongruity with the essential constituents of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the character's life and possible associations fit the poem's aims; the critic should weigh the character's fit with genre expectations and poetic purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's duty to select dignified and happy attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: The office and duty of the poet is to select the most dignified as well as 'the gayest, happiest attitude of things.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reverse (burlesque, travesty, predominant taste for low forms) is appropriate to different genres and is deemed indicative of low or degraded taste in a poet aiming at lofty composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mannerism and abrupt stylistic transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A fault is the mannerism of style: sudden and unprepared transitions from lines or sentences of peculiar felicity to a style unimpassioned and undistinguished—sinking into prose-like language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should note sudden drops in style and whether passages of striking originality are followed by neutral or prosaic language without preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix incompatible registers without preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternating dissimilar states of feeling (poetic vs. prose registers, or insertion of songs/arias at inappropriate points) is unpleasant and can break reader expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain structural placement (e.g., place arias at ends of scenes as Metastasio did) and raise surrounding style appropriately to avoid awkward juxtapositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain harmonious diction, imagery, and unity of tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity arises when passages of sudden superiority or different diction interrupt the surrounding context; repetition of the same image too close together can also be jarring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet should ensure images and diction are congruent across neighboring passages so the reader experiences a harmonious whole rather than anticlimax or hyperclimax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect metrical preparation and reader expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The pleasure of poetic writing partly derives from preparation and previous expectation; metre and elevated diction prime the reader—failure to prepare yields disappointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defects occur frequently, the metre merely reminds the reader of claims it fails to satisfy; frequent defects lead to alternating feelings of anticlimax and hyperclimax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge before fully reading the work
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic should not compose a critique prior to reading the work and then hunt for passages to support preconceived opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practice leads to unfair and misleading criticism; the critic must read and consider the whole before forming and presenting judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge truths within a mistaken theory
rubrics_metrics.description: When refuting a poet's theoretical principles, give due credit to the portion and importance of truths blended within that theory and substitute more philosophical principles where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A measured confutation both corrects errors and recognizes genuine insights so as not to throw out valuable elements with mistaken extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish occasional defects from characteristic failings
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether defects are merely occasional (isolated) or characteristic of a poet's theory and practice; identify whether faults are essential to the poet's manner or episodic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples and frequency counts where possible; show whether defects are inherent (woven into the fabric) or sporadic and separable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid moral invective disguised as aesthetic judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that consigns an author to the 'house of incurables' or employs moralized contempt without argumentative basis is condemned; the critic's state of taste and sensibility may be at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep aesthetic judgments grounded in argument and evidence rather than moral denunciation or ranting contempt.
